missionPremise: Flip the flood rail from legacy (fema-nfhl-bulk-v1 tile-centre NFHL lookups, measured median 227m / max 366m from the actual parcel, retired at the tier2-bake layer 2026-08-19 per SS-W16/P-45 but still the flood serve path for un-slated counties) to parcel_record (point-on-surface NFHL join, PARCEL-C-REPORT's own already-tested reader) across all six program counties, mirroring PARCEL-B-SLATE1's cutover mechanism exactly. Distinct from slate-1 in one deliberate way: Caldwell (48055) is included in this card's slate even though its own gate verdict is 'excluded' (a known geometry/coverage gap for Caldwell specifically), so that the allowlist's 'refused' state -- attempted-and-declined, visible, distinct from a silently-unslated pair's default 'legacy' -- would be captured live and observed at the wire for the first time in this card family, rather than only reasoned about from the allowlist's own logic.
completionPredicate: Met in full. All six counties resolved correctly: five (48021 Bastrop, 48209 Hays, 48309 McLennan, 48453 Travis, 48491 Williamson) carry a real 'pass' verdict in parcel_gate_verdict (unaccounted_count 0 across the board) and serve floodHazardFact via sourceAdapter=parcel_record in production. The sixth (48055 Caldwell) carries an 'excluded' verdict and correctly falls back to the legacy fema-nfhl-bulk-v1 adapter in production -- the owed live-refused capture this card's premise specifically asked for, now actually observed rather than only inferred from resolveAllowlistState's logic. Both named acceptance probes pass exactly as specified: gold 48021:34137 serves floodZone=X; the AO/AE discriminator 48021:36521 serves floodZone=AE with inSpecialFloodHazardArea=true. This is a FULL retirement of this card's scope -- unlike PARCEL-B-SLATE1, which closed with two of five rails (valueHistory, and the flood rail this card now owns) explicitly still open.

criticalFindingsThisCard.finding: Base-move mid-merge: PR #592 was fully CI-green but origin/main advanced (the concurrent property-seat session's PR #593, PARCEL-B-SLATE2) before merge. GitHub reported mergeable/BEHIND with no textual conflict, but the standing re-green-against-current-base rule required a local merge + fresh typecheck + fresh DB-backed test run before trusting it, rather than accepting GitHub's own auto-merge claim. The local merge was clean at the git level (no conflict markers on the two shared route files) but that alone does not prove semantic correctness -- verified separately via a real pgvector-enabled local postgres (found an existing p106-pg container already running with the vector extension available, matching CI's own postgres:test_db pattern) and a full re-run of every merge-touched test file. Zero regressions found, but the check was real, not assumed.
criticalFindingsThisCard.disposition: resolved -- merged clean, re-verified, re-pushed, CI re-confirmed green on the merge commit before the actual PR merge.
